w10_T4_003176: Priya had 98 trading cards, while her cousin Marcus had only 61, so Priya's pile was clearly the bigger one. At a weekend fair Priya bought 39 more cards, and a friend then gave her another 9. Later she sold 96 of her cards to a dealer. In the club tournament, every card a player still holds scores 3 points per round, and the tournament ran for 6 rounds. How many points did Priya's cards score in total over the tournament?
w10_T4_003177: In the morning, Rosa's jam company loaded 72 crates onto each of its 8 delivery trucks, and every crate held 9 jars of jam. In the afternoon all of the jars were repacked at the market into gift boxes of 6 jars each. Each gift box sold for 8 dollars, and every box was sold; the market's card reader reports takings in cents, so Rosa converted the total into dollars before writing it down. In the evening she paid 3388 dollars for the day's fuel, rent and wages out of those takings. How many dollars did Rosa have left from the day's takings after paying those costs?
w10_T4_003179: Lena tracked her score through a whole run of the arcade game Star Vault. She scored 152 points on each of the first 6 levels. A hidden chest then added 41 points to her score. Picking up a double-score token doubled her entire score. On the final level every point she had became worth 9 points on the final scoreboard. The leaderboard displays scores in thousands, so Lena converted her own tally from single points to read her place on it. How many points did Lena's score show on the final scoreboard?
w10_T4_003180: Early in the morning, Hana's flower stall had 64 tulips. A delivery brought 38 more tulips, and she cut 4 more from her own garden. In the afternoon she sold every tulip she had at 9 dollars each. In the evening a regular customer handed her a 40-dollar tip on top of her sales. How many dollars did Hana take in that day, including the tip?
w10_T4_003189: Omar keeps a log of every kilometre he drives for the courier firm. Each delivery run is 197 kilometres, he makes 4 runs a day, and he worked 7 days straight. A road closure then added a 45-kilometre detour to his log. His manager pointed out that his colleague Ben had logged only 3200 kilometres, far less than Omar. For the payroll report the firm doubles every driver's logged distance to account for the empty return legs. How many kilometres does Omar's log show on the payroll report?
w10_T4_003190: Nadia sells cookies from a market stall and tracks her share of the money carefully. On Monday she baked 76 cookies and then a second batch of 37 more, and she sold every one of them at 9 dollars apiece. She took in exactly the same amount on each of the 7 days of the market week. The week's takings were split equally among the 3 partners who run the stall, Nadia being one of them. Her friend Felix, who runs the stall next door and makes barely a dozen sales a day, always ends up with less than Nadia. From her share Nadia paid 2114 dollars for the stall's rent. How many dollars did Nadia have left from her share after paying the rent?
w10_T4_003191: Kai keeps a running total of the minutes he has read this week, and he insists on keeping it in minutes even though his reading app converts the total into hours on its summary screen. On Monday the total stood at 16 minutes. He read for 55 minutes on Tuesday, 63 minutes on Wednesday, 55 minutes on Thursday and 26 minutes on Friday. His sister Mia, who kept the same kind of log, finished the week with a smaller total than Kai. How many minutes did Kai's running total show at the end of Friday?
w10_T4_003193: In the morning, Bruno had 50 crates at his farm stand, but 29 of them were empty, so he set those aside and kept only the full ones. Each full crate held 4 watermelons. In the afternoon a neighbour dropped off 73 more watermelons for him to sell. In the evening, at the festival, Bruno cut every watermelon into 7 slices and sold each slice for 8 dollars, selling all of them. How many dollars did Bruno make from the slices?
w10_T4_003194: Ana started the day with 27 marbles, and her brother handed her 27 more. She divided all of them into 3 equal jars, kept one jar for herself and gave the other jars away. Later she bought 28 marbles at a shop and received 15 as a gift. At the end of the day she traded every marble she had to a collector for 6 cents each; the collector quoted the total in dollars, but Ana converted it back into cents. She then split that money equally among 3 people: herself, Leo and Sam, with Leo grumbling that his own collection had earned him less than Ana's had. How many cents did Ana keep?
w10_T4_003195: The Hillcrest orchard has 68 apple trees in each of its 6 rows. This year every tree yielded 9 baskets of apples. The orchard also has 25 pear trees, which are not being harvested yet. The picking crew works for half a day before stopping for lunch. The apple baskets were packed 3 to a crate, and every crate sold to the wholesaler for 6 dollars. How many dollars did the orchard receive for the apple crates?
w10_T4_003198: A bottling line fills 136 bottles every minute, and it ran for 9 minutes before the first break. The bottles were packed into cases of 6 bottles each. The plant employs 14 workers on this line. To the cases from the run, the foreman added 70 cases left from yesterday and 72 cases from a second line. Each case weighs 3 kilograms; the floor scale reads in grams, so the foreman converted the case weight into kilograms before doing his sums. How many kilograms did all the cases together weigh?
w10_T4_003199: In the morning Jun had 68 dollars, and his grandmother matched it so that he had twice as much. He then spent 112 dollars on a jacket. In the afternoon he earned 64 dollars washing cars. In the evening at the airport he exchanged all of his dollars for pesos at 6 pesos per dollar. He then paid 429 pesos for a taxi. How many pesos did Jun have left?
w10_T4_003200: A small cafe bought 160 eggs and used an equal number on each of 5 days. Each egg made one omelette, and every omelette sold for 9 dollars, so the cafe sold that many omelettes on the fifth day. The cafe has 12 tables. On the fifth day it also took 43 dollars for coffee and 41 dollars for pastries; the till records everything in cents, but the owner converts the figures to dollars for her notebook. That evening she paid 60 dollars for the milk delivery out of the day's money. How many dollars did the cafe have left from the fifth day's takings?
w10_T4_003203: Dev arrived at the arcade with 101 tokens. He used 94 tokens on racing games and then 6 more on a claw machine. He fed his last token into a ticket machine that pays out 9 tickets per token. A lucky spin then doubled his tickets, leaving him with twice as many. Each ticket is worth 5 cents at the prize counter; the price board there is written in dollars, so Dev converted the prices into cents to compare. He spent 17 cents' worth of tickets on a sticker, while his friend Nia, who had played beside him, was left with fewer cents' worth of tickets than Dev. How many cents' worth of tickets did Dev have left?
w10_T4_003211: Ines runs a small textile workshop. She received 5 rolls of linen, each 73 metres long; the supplier lists lengths in centimetres, so she converted them to metres for her records. She used 119 metres of the linen on a large curtain order. From every remaining metre she cut 3 scarves, and she added 78 scarves from last month's stock. She packed all the scarves into boxes of 6 and shipped 63 boxes to a boutique. How many boxes of scarves did Ines still have?
w10_T4_003224: A seed company puts 144 grams of seed in each tray, with 6 trays on every rack, 6 racks in every greenhouse, and 3 greenhouses in use. The greenhouses are kept at 24 degrees. The grower also had 44 grams of spare seed in a jar, which he added to the total. The supplier's invoice is written in kilograms, so the grower converted everything to grams to check it. When soaked overnight, the seed swells to twice its dry weight. How many grams did all the soaked seed weigh?
w10_T4_003228: Mara had 103 glass beads for a necklace. She lost 22 of them when the bag split, found 11 more under the sofa, and gave 7 to her cousin Tobias. Each of her remaining beads weighs 8 grams. She threaded them all onto a chain with a 40-gram clasp and 3 grams of silk cord. Tobias made his own necklace, but it weighed less than Mara's. How many grams did Mara's finished necklace weigh?
w10_T4_003235: Ivan tracked the money in his charity raffle fund from start to finish. Each ticket cost 76 cents plus a 29-cent handling fee, and Ivan added everything to the fund in cents even though the bank statement shows dollars. Every family bought 5 tickets, there were 7 families on each street, and Ivan covered 5 streets. He found a 13-cent coin at the bottom of the collection box and added it to the fund. His co-organiser Petra, who ran a separate fund, collected less than Ivan. Ivan then paid 2986 cents from the fund for printing. How many cents were in Ivan's fund after paying for printing?
w10_T4_003238: Zoe walks dogs for 25 dollars a walk. She does 7 walks each week and worked for 5 weeks. She usually walks 4 dogs at a time. A grateful owner gave her a 55-dollar bonus. Her booking app reports earnings in cents, so Zoe converted the amount to dollars before paying her bills. She then paid 560 dollars in rent and 246 dollars for leads and treats. How many dollars did Zoe have left?
w10_T4_003242: Leila's flock started the year at 163 sheep. In spring 14 lambs were born, then she sold 4 old ewes, and later she bought 14 sheep at auction. Her neighbour Hamid's flock of 120 sheep is smaller than Leila's. At shearing time every sheep in Leila's flock gave 5 kilograms of wool. How many kilograms of wool did Leila's flock produce?
w10_T4_003244: A village pump was installed a dozen years ago and moved 99 litres of water per hour. A new motor raised its flow by 18 litres per hour, a wider pipe added 36 litres per hour, and a second inlet added another 59 litres per hour. The pump then ran at that final rate for 8 hours a day for 7 days. How many litres of water did the pump move in those 7 days?
w10_T4_003245: Farah took 232 photos on her trip and found 51 more on her old camera. She ordered 4 prints of every photo; the print shop quotes prices in cents, so she converted the bill into dollars. She sorted all the prints into 4 equal stacks and kept 1 stack, giving the other stacks to relatives. She then sold each print in her stack for 4 dollars at a craft fair. Her brother Karim sold prints at the same fair but earned less than Farah. How many dollars did Farah earn from her prints?
w10_T4_003247: In the morning a fishing boat returned to harbour with 151 crates of mackerel, and the crew found 8 more crates stowed in the hold. Each crate held 9 kilograms of fish. The boat has a crew of 5. In the afternoon a second short trip brought in 50 more kilograms of fish. In the evening the whole catch sold at the fish market for 7 dollars per kilogram. How many dollars did the catch sell for?
w10_T4_003251: Rina planned 27 minutes of running each day but cut 10 minutes from it. She added 50 minutes of cycling and 8 minutes of stretching to her daily routine. Her watch reports her training time in hours, but she logs everything in minutes. She followed this daily routine for 7 days. On the last day she also went on a 60-minute hike. How many minutes of training did Rina log in total?
w10_T4_003254: Ben had 50 stickers and gave half of them to his sister. He is 9 years old. At the school swap table he traded each remaining sticker for 3 cards. He then bought 77 more cards at the shop. He gave 142 cards to the charity drive. How many cards did Ben have left?
